headline: Eighth Army grinds into Axis minefields at El Alamein
detail: Second night of Montgomery's offensive. Infantry and sappers clear lanes under fire while armour queues behind, in the dust and the dark.

headline: Japanese assault on Henderson Field fails on Guadalcanal
detail: Wave after wave of Japanese infantry break against Marine and Army lines around the airfield. The Americans hold, and their aircraft keep flying.

headline: USS Hornet sunk at the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands
detail: Japanese carrier aircraft sink the carrier Hornet and damage Enterprise, but lose so many experienced aircrew that the victory costs Japan dearly.

headline: Operation Supercharge breaks the Axis line at Alamein
detail: A fresh British assault punches through the Axis defences near Tel el Aqqaqir. Rommel's armour is reduced to a few dozen tanks.

headline: Rommel retreats from El Alamein
detail: Defying Hitler's order to stand fast, Rommel pulls his army west. Some 30,000 Axis soldiers are left behind as prisoners.

headline: Operation Torch: Allied armies land in Morocco and Algeria
detail: More than 100,000 American and British troops come ashore at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers. Vichy French forces resist for up to three days.

headline: Churchill calls Alamein "the end of the beginning"
detail: At the Lord Mayor's luncheon at the Mansion House, Churchill tells Britain the tide may be turning, but warns the war is far from over.

headline: Germany occupies Vichy France
detail: After Darlan's ceasefire in North Africa, German and Italian troops pour into France's unoccupied southern zone. Vichy's pretence of independence ends.

headline: Five Sullivan brothers die as USS Juneau is sunk
detail: In the Naval Battle of Guadalcanal the cruiser Juneau is torpedoed. All five Sullivan brothers of Waterloo, Iowa, are among nearly 700 dead.

headline: Church bells ring across Britain for Alamein
detail: For the first time since 1940, when bells were kept silent as an invasion alarm, churches ring out to mark the desert victory.

headline: Operation Uranus: Red Army strikes at Stalingrad's flanks
detail: At 07:20, in freezing fog, some 3,500 Soviet guns open fire on the Romanian Third Army northwest of Stalingrad.

headline: German Sixth Army trapped at Stalingrad
detail: Soviet pincers meet near Kalach on the Don, encircling roughly 250,000 to 300,000 Axis soldiers between the Don and the Volga.

headline: The Donau sails from Oslo with Norway's Jews
detail: The transport ship carries 529 Norwegian Jews, arrested by Norwegian police, to Stettin and on to Auschwitz. Only nine will survive.

headline: French fleet scuttled at Toulon
detail: As German troops storm the naval base, French crews sink 77 vessels, including three battleships and seven cruisers, rather than surrender them.

headline: Cocoanut Grove nightclub fire kills 492 in Boston
detail: Fire races through a crowded Boston nightclub, many of its guests servicemen on leave. Locked and blocked exits turn it into a death trap.

headline: Beveridge Report published in Britain
detail: Sir William Beveridge proposes social insurance "from cradle to grave". Queues form to buy the report; it sells hundreds of thousands of copies.

headline: First self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, Chicago
detail: Enrico Fermi's team brings Chicago Pile-1, a stack of graphite and uranium under a stadium stand, to criticality. It produces about half a watt.

headline: Royal Marine canoeists mine ships in Bordeaux harbour
detail: Operation Frankton: two canoes of the original five reach Bordeaux and fix limpets to six ships. Only Hasler and Sparks will survive.

headline: Manstein's relief attempt for Stalingrad begins
detail: Operation Winter Storm drives northeast towards the Stalingrad pocket. It gets within about 50 kilometres before being stopped.

headline: Operation Little Saturn smashes the Italian Eighth Army
detail: A new Soviet offensive on the middle Don routs the Italian army and threatens the airfields supplying the Stalingrad pocket.

headline: Allies publicly condemn Germany's extermination of the Jews
detail: Eden reads a joint declaration of eleven Allied governments in the Commons. Members stand in silence. No rescue plan follows.

headline: Admiral Darlan assassinated in Algiers
detail: The Vichy admiral the Allies had accepted as French leader in North Africa is shot by a young monarchist, Fernand Bonnier de La Chapelle.

headline: Battle of the Barents Sea: German raiders driven off
detail: British destroyers defend Arctic convoy JW 51B against the cruiser Hipper and the pocket battleship Lützow. A furious Hitler turns on his surface fleet.

headline: Buna falls in Papua
detail: Australian and American troops take the Japanese stronghold at Buna after weeks of fighting in swamp and jungle, in heat and sickness.

headline: Red Army begins crushing the Stalingrad pocket
detail: Operation Ring opens with a massive barrage. Paulus has rejected a call to surrender; his starving men are pushed back street by street.

headline: US and Britain give up special rights in China
detail: New treaties end a century of extraterritoriality, under which foreigners in China answered only to their own courts.

headline: Roosevelt and Churchill meet at Casablanca
detail: The Casablanca Conference opens at the Anfa Hotel. Stalin declines to attend; he has a battle to finish.

headline: Siege of Leningrad broken by a land corridor
detail: Operation Iskra links the Leningrad and Volkhov Fronts south of Lake Ladoga, opening a narrow strip of land to the starving city.

headline: First armed Jewish resistance in the Warsaw ghetto
detail: When German forces begin a new round of deportations, Jewish fighters open fire. The Germans halt the action after four days.

headline: German bomb kills 38 children at a London school
detail: In a daylight raid a bomb hits Sandhurst Road School in Catford. Thirty-eight children and six staff are killed.

headline: Roosevelt demands "unconditional surrender"
detail: At the closing press conference in Casablanca, Roosevelt announces that the Allies will accept nothing less from Germany, Italy and Japan.

headline: US bombers strike Germany for the first time
detail: Eighth Air Force B-17s and B-24s attack the naval base at Wilhelmshaven in the first American raid on German soil.

headline: Mosquitos disrupt Göring's Berlin anniversary speech
detail: On the tenth anniversary of Hitler taking power, RAF Mosquitos bomb Berlin in daylight, knocking Göring's live broadcast off the air.

headline: Paulus surrenders at Stalingrad
detail: Promoted to field marshal the day before, Friedrich Paulus gives himself up in the cellar of a Stalingrad department store.

headline: Battle of Stalingrad ends
detail: The last German troops in the northern pocket surrender. About 91,000 men go into captivity; only some 5,000 will ever return home.

headline: Germany announces Stalingrad defeat; three days of mourning
detail: State radio admits the loss of the Sixth Army. Theatres and cinemas close as the country is ordered into national mourning.

headline: Wingate's Chindits march into Burma
detail: Operation Longcloth begins: some 3,000 men in columns, supplied by air, set out to raid deep behind Japanese lines.

headline: Guadalcanal declared secure
detail: Six months after the landings, the Japanese have evacuated their last troops by night. Japan has lost thousands of men, ships and aircraft.

headline: Red Army liberates Kharkov
detail: Soviet troops retake Ukraine's second city. Within a month a German counter-stroke under Manstein will capture it again.

headline: Goebbels declares "total war" in Berlin
detail: In the Sportpalast, before a hand-picked crowd, Goebbels demands total mobilisation. The same morning, Hans and Sophie Scholl are arrested in Munich.

headline: Americans routed at the Kasserine Pass
detail: Rommel's counter-attack in Tunisia throws back inexperienced US troops. Within days the line is restored, and the Americans learn fast.

headline: White Rose students executed in Munich
detail: Hans and Sophie Scholl and Christoph Probst are guillotined at Stadelheim prison hours after their trial before the People's Court.

headline: Berlin round-up seizes the city's last Jewish workers
detail: Thousands of Jewish forced labourers are arrested at their workplaces for deportation. Non-Jewish wives gather outside the Rosenstrasse building where their husbands are held.

headline: Norwegian saboteurs wreck the Vemork heavy-water plant
detail: Operation Gunnerside: commandos enter the plant at Rjukan, destroy the heavy-water cells and escape without a shot fired.

headline: Battle of the Bismarck Sea
detail: Allied aircraft destroy a Japanese convoy bound for Lae, sinking all eight transports and four destroyers. Nearly 3,000 men die.

headline: 173 crushed to death at Bethnal Green tube shelter
detail: Panic on a dark, wet stairway during an air-raid alert kills 173 people, many of them children. No bomb has fallen.

headline: Britain's first jet fighter, the Gloster Meteor, flies
detail: A Meteor prototype powered by two de Havilland Halford engines takes off from RAF Cranwell. It will be the only Allied jet to fly combat operations in the war.

headline: Rosenstrasse men released after their wives' protest
detail: Goebbels orders the release of the Jewish husbands held in Berlin's Rosenstrasse, after a week of public protest by their non-Jewish wives.

headline: Kraków ghetto liquidated
detail: SS and police clear the ghetto over two days. Thousands are marched to Płaszów camp, many are shot in the streets, and others are deported to Auschwitz.

headline: Deportation of Thessaloniki's Jews begins
detail: The first train leaves the Greek port city for Auschwitz. Within five months nearly the whole of its ancient Sephardic community is gone.

headline: Manstein retakes Kharkov
detail: The Third Battle of Kharkov ends with the city back in German hands, stabilising the southern front after the Stalingrad disaster.

headline: Largest convoy battle of the war
detail: Around convoys HX 229 and SC 122, about forty U-boats sink 22 merchant ships in four days, for the loss of one submarine.

headline: Khatyn burned with its people inside
detail: In Belarus, a German-commanded police battalion and the SS Dirlewanger unit murder the 149 inhabitants of Khatyn, many of them children.

headline: Japanese air offensive strikes Guadalcanal
detail: In Operation I-Go, Yamamoto throws carrier and land-based aircraft against Allied shipping in the Solomons. The raids do far less damage than Tokyo believes.

headline: Germany announces mass graves at Katyn
detail: German radio reports the graves of thousands of Polish officers near Smolensk. They were shot by the Soviet NKVD in 1940; Moscow blames Germany.

headline: Admiral Yamamoto shot down over Bougainville
detail: US P-38 fighters, guided by decrypted Japanese signals, intercept and destroy the bomber carrying the commander of Japan's Combined Fleet.

headline: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising begins
detail: On the eve of Passover, Jewish fighters meet German deportation forces with gunfire. The SS respond by burning the ghetto block by block.

headline: Bermuda Conference on refugees opens
detail: British and American officials meet to discuss refugees from Nazi Europe. Twelve days of talks produce almost nothing.

headline: Belgian resistance fighters stop a train bound for Auschwitz
detail: Three young men armed with one pistol halt the twentieth convoy from Mechelen. Several prisoners escape into the night; others jump from the moving train.

headline: Roosevelt reveals Japan executed captured Doolittle raiders
detail: The President announces that Japan tried and executed some of the airmen captured after the April 1942 Tokyo raid. Americans are enraged.

headline: Moscow breaks with the Polish government in London
detail: Stalin severs relations after the Polish government asks the International Red Cross to investigate Katyn.

headline: A body carrying false plans washes ashore at Huelva
detail: Operation Mincemeat: a corpse dressed as a Royal Marines officer carries letters pointing to Allied landings in Greece and Sardinia, not Sicily.

headline: Tunis and Bizerte fall to the Allies
detail: British troops enter Tunis and Americans take Bizerte. The Axis bridgehead in Africa collapses into the Cape Bon peninsula.

headline: Axis forces in North Africa surrender
detail: About a quarter of a million German and Italian soldiers become prisoners. The war in Africa is over.

headline: Hospital ship Centaur sunk off Queensland
detail: A Japanese submarine torpedoes the Australian hospital ship, clearly marked with red crosses. 268 of the 332 people aboard die.

headline: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising crushed; Great Synagogue blown up
detail: Jürgen Stroop reports that the Jewish quarter of Warsaw "no longer exists". At least 13,000 Jews died in the fighting.

headline: Dambusters breach the Möhne and Eder dams
detail: Lancasters of 617 Squadron burst two Ruhr dams. About 1,600 people drown, around a thousand of them foreign forced labourers.

headline: Stalin announces the dissolution of the Comintern
detail: The Communist International is wound up, a gesture to reassure Stalin's Western allies.

headline: Dönitz withdraws U-boats from the North Atlantic
detail: After losing 41 submarines in "Black May", Germany admits defeat in the convoy battle, for now.

headline: Last Japanese charge on Attu
detail: The Japanese garrison on the Aleutian island makes a final suicidal attack. Of some 2,400 defenders, only 28 are taken alive.

headline: Airliner carrying actor Leslie Howard shot down
detail: German fighters destroy BOAC Flight 777 over the Bay of Biscay on its way from Lisbon to Bristol. All seventeen aboard die.

headline: Zoot Suit Riots erupt in Los Angeles
detail: Servicemen roam the city beating young Mexican-Americans in "zoot suits". The violence lasts several days; police mostly arrest the victims.

headline: Allies order Operation Pointblank
detail: A new directive makes the destruction of the German fighter force and aircraft industry the first aim of the bomber offensive.

headline: Pantelleria surrenders after heavy bombing
detail: The Italian island fortress between Tunisia and Sicily gives up after days of air and naval bombardment, as British troops come ashore.

headline: Race riot in Detroit leaves 34 dead
detail: Three days of violence in the wartime arsenal city end only when federal troops arrive. Most of the dead are Black residents.

headline: Jean Moulin arrested by the Gestapo
detail: De Gaulle's envoy, who united the French Resistance, is betrayed and seized at Caluire, near Lyon. He dies after torture weeks later.

headline: US Congress curbs wartime strikes over Roosevelt's veto
detail: After a coal miners' strike, the Smith-Connally Act lets the government seize struck war plants and bans strikes in them.

headline: Americans land in the New Georgia islands
detail: Operation Cartwheel advances in the Solomons with landings on Rendova, aimed at the Japanese airfield at Munda.

headline: General Sikorski killed in Gibraltar air crash
detail: The Polish prime minister and commander-in-chief dies with his daughter when his Liberator crashes on take-off. Only the Czech pilot survives.

headline: Battle of Kursk begins
detail: Germany launches Operation Citadel against the Kursk salient. The forewarned Red Army waits behind defences nearly 300 kilometres deep.

headline: Allies invade Sicily
detail: Operation Husky lands British, Canadian and American divisions along the southern coast of Sicily, the largest seaborne landing yet.

headline: Tank battle at Prokhorovka
detail: The Soviet 5th Guards Tank Army counter-attacks the SS panzer corps. Soviet losses are heavy, but the German southern drive is stopped.

headline: Hitler calls off the Kursk offensive
detail: With the Allies ashore in Sicily and Soviet attacks breaking out at Orel, Hitler halts Operation Citadel. Germany will never again attack on this scale in the east.

headline: Allied bombers strike Rome for the first time
detail: American bombers hit the rail yards of San Lorenzo. More than a thousand civilians die. Pope Pius XII visits the ruins.

headline: Mussolini overthrown and arrested
detail: After the Fascist Grand Council votes against him, King Victor Emmanuel III dismisses Mussolini. Marshal Badoglio forms a new government.

headline: Firestorm engulfs Hamburg
detail: The RAF raid of 27-28 July creates a firestorm in Hamburg's eastern districts. Operation Gomorrah kills some 37,000 people.

headline: US bombers attack the Ploiești oil refineries
detail: Operation Tidal Wave sends 177 Liberators at treetop height against Romania's oil fields. Fifty-three are lost, and production soon recovers.

headline: Prisoners revolt at Treblinka
detail: Inmates of the death camp seize weapons and set fire to buildings. About 200 escape; fewer than a hundred survive the pursuit.

headline: PT-109 sunk; Lieutenant John F. Kennedy saves his crew
detail: A Japanese destroyer rams the torpedo boat in the Solomons. Kennedy leads the survivors to an island, towing an injured man by his lifejacket strap.

headline: Soviet partisans launch the "rail war"
detail: Partisan brigades across occupied Belorussia blow up tens of thousands of rails to cripple German supply lines behind the front.

headline: Orel and Belgorod liberated
detail: Moscow marks the victories with its first artillery salute of the war: twelve salvoes from 120 guns.

headline: Americans land on Kiska and find it empty
detail: US and Canadian troops storm the Aleutian island to discover the Japanese garrison slipped away under cover of fog two weeks earlier.

headline: Uprising in the Białystok ghetto
detail: Jewish fighters resist the final liquidation of the ghetto with a handful of weapons. The revolt is crushed within days.

headline: Sicily falls; Germans escape across the strait
detail: American troops enter Messina. More than 100,000 German and Italian soldiers have already been ferried to the mainland.

headline: Heavy US losses over Schweinfurt and Regensburg
detail: The Eighth Air Force loses 60 bombers attacking ball-bearing and aircraft factories, proof that unescorted daylight raids cannot last.

headline: RAF bombs the Peenemünde rocket centre
detail: Nearly 600 bombers strike the V-2 research site. At least 500 forced labourers die in a camp hit by mistake.

headline: Red Army takes Kharkov for good
detail: Ukraine's second city is liberated for the second and final time, completing the Soviet counter-offensive after Kursk.

headline: Quebec Conference ends
detail: Roosevelt and Churchill confirm May 1944 for the invasion of France and agree to pool atomic research.

headline: Germany imposes martial law in Denmark
detail: The Danish government resigns rather than accept death sentences for saboteurs. The navy scuttles its ships in Copenhagen.

headline: Italy signs armistice; British land in Calabria
detail: General Castellano signs at Cassibile in Sicily. Montgomery's Eighth Army crosses the Strait of Messina to the mainland.

headline: Italy's surrender announced
detail: Eisenhower broadcasts the armistice; Badoglio confirms it. The King and government flee Rome the next morning.

headline: Allies land at Salerno; battleship Roma sunk
detail: The US Fifth Army lands in the Gulf of Salerno. German bombers sink the Roma with a guided bomb; nearly 1,400 of her crew die.

headline: German paratroopers free Mussolini
detail: Gliders land beside the Gran Sasso hotel where he is held. Hitler installs him as head of a puppet republic in the north.

headline: X-craft midget submarines cripple the Tirpitz
detail: Two British midget submarines lay charges under the battleship in Kaafjord, Norway, putting her out of action for months.

headline: Italian soldiers massacred on Cephalonia
detail: After the Acqui Division surrenders to German forces, more than 5,000 Italian prisoners are executed over the following days.

headline: Smolensk liberated
detail: The Red Army retakes the ruined city after more than two years of German occupation.

headline: Commandos raid Singapore harbour in canoes
detail: Operation Jaywick: six men from the fishing boat Krait fix limpet mines to Japanese ships. All return safely to Australia.

headline: Neapolitans drive the Germans out of Naples
detail: After four days of street fighting by civilians, students and boys, the German garrison withdraws. Allied troops enter on 1 October.

headline: Danish Jews escape to Sweden by fishing boat
detail: Warned of the round-up, ordinary Danes hide their Jewish neighbours. Over three weeks about 7,500 are ferried across the Øresund.

headline: Himmler speaks openly of extermination at Posen
detail: In a secret speech to SS officers, Himmler describes the murder of the Jews as a "glorious page" of history that must never be written.

headline: Kempeitai's "Double Tenth" arrests in Singapore
detail: Blaming civilian internees for the Jaywick raid, Japanese military police arrest and torture 57 people. Fifteen die.

headline: Italy declares war on Germany
detail: Badoglio's government, now in the Allied-held south, becomes a co-belligerent against its former ally.

headline: Sobibor prisoners revolt
detail: Eleven SS men are killed and about 300 prisoners break out. Roughly 60 will survive the war. The camp is then dismantled.

headline: "Black Thursday" over Schweinfurt
detail: The Eighth Air Force loses 60 bombers on a second raid against the ball-bearing plants. Deep unescorted raids are suspended.

headline: SS round up the Jews of Rome
detail: In a single morning, more than a thousand Jews are seized in Rome's old ghetto and elsewhere. Two days later they are deported to Auschwitz.

headline: Burma-Thailand "Death Railway" completed
detail: The two halves of the line meet. Its building has cost the lives of over 12,000 Allied prisoners and many tens of thousands of Asian labourers.

headline: Wavell becomes Viceroy as famine ravages Bengal
detail: Lord Wavell takes office in India. Within weeks he sends the army to carry food into Bengal, where millions are dying.

headline: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaims a Free India government
detail: In Japanese-occupied Singapore, the Indian nationalist announces a provisional government and commands the Indian National Army.

headline: Allied foreign ministers issue the Moscow Declarations
detail: Britain, the US and the USSR promise that German war criminals will be sent back to stand trial where their crimes were committed.

headline: US Marines land on Bougainville
detail: The 3rd Marine Division comes ashore at Empress Augusta Bay to build airfields within range of Rabaul.

headline: Japanese offensive against Changde begins
detail: Some 60,000 Japanese troops attack the rice-trade city of Changde in Hunan. Chinese defenders fight house to house; the battle lasts weeks.

headline: Operation Harvest Festival: mass shootings at Majdanek
detail: Over two days SS and police shoot about 42,000 Jews at Majdanek, Trawniki and Poniatowa, to music played over loudspeakers.

headline: Oak Ridge reactor goes critical
detail: The X-10 Graphite Reactor in Tennessee becomes the world's second reactor and the first built for continuous operation, producing plutonium for research.

headline: Japan hosts the Greater East Asia Conference
detail: Leaders of Japan's puppet and allied states meet in Tokyo to proclaim a "co-prosperity" that occupied Asia experiences as forced labour and requisition.

headline: Red Army liberates Kiev
detail: Soviet troops retake the Ukrainian capital, where the Babi Yar ravine holds the bodies of tens of thousands murdered in 1941.

headline: RAF opens the Battle of Berlin
detail: Bomber Command begins a winter campaign against the German capital. It will cost over a thousand bombers without breaking the city.

headline: US Marines land on Tarawa
detail: On Betio, a reef stops the landing craft and Marines wade ashore under fire. More than a thousand Americans die in 76 hours.

headline: Roosevelt, Churchill and Chiang meet in Cairo
detail: The Cairo Conference promises that territories Japan seized from China, including Manchuria and Taiwan, will be returned.

headline: The Big Three meet in Tehran
detail: Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill meet together for the first time. The invasion of France is promised for May 1944.

headline: Tito's partisans proclaim a new Yugoslavia
detail: At Jajce, the partisan assembly AVNOJ forms a provisional government and bars the exiled king from returning.

headline: German raid on Bari releases mustard gas
detail: German bombers hit the crowded harbour, sinking 27 ships. A secret American cargo of mustard gas poisons sailors and townspeople.

headline: Germans massacre the men of Kalavryta
detail: In reprisal for the killing of German prisoners by Greek partisans, troops shoot nearly 500 men and boys and burn the town.

headline: Americans land at Arawe on New Britain
detail: US troops go ashore on the island's south coast, the first step in the campaign to isolate the Japanese base at Rabaul.

headline: US repeals the Chinese Exclusion Act
detail: Congress ends sixty years of barring Chinese immigrants, a gesture to a wartime ally. The new quota is just 105 people a year.

headline: Eisenhower named to command the invasion of Europe
detail: Roosevelt announces in a Christmas Eve broadcast that Eisenhower will be Supreme Commander for the landings in France.

headline: Red Army opens new offensive west of Kiev
detail: The Zhitomir-Berdichev offensive pushes the Germans back across western Ukraine in midwinter.

headline: Scharnhorst sunk off the North Cape
detail: The battleship Duke of York and her escorts sink the German battlecruiser in Arctic darkness. Only 36 of nearly 2,000 men survive.

headline: US Marines land at Cape Gloucester
detail: The 1st Marine Division lands on western New Britain to tighten the ring around the Japanese base at Rabaul.

headline: Canadians take Ortona after a week of street fighting
detail: The 1st Canadian Division clears the Adriatic town house by house, mouse-holing through walls under German fire.

headline: Americans land at Saidor in New Guinea
detail: A landing on the north coast cuts off the line of retreat of Japanese troops falling back from the Huon Peninsula.

headline: Count Ciano executed in Verona
detail: Mussolini's son-in-law and former foreign minister, who voted against him in the Grand Council, is shot by a Fascist firing squad.

headline: Red Army opens the offensive to free Leningrad
detail: The Leningrad and Volkhov Fronts attack the German Eighteenth Army, which has besieged the city since 1941.

headline: Luftwaffe begins the "Baby Blitz" on London
detail: Operation Steinbock sends German bombers back over England in a final winter campaign of night raids on London.

headline: Allies land at Anzio
detail: Some 36,000 troops come ashore behind the Gustav Line almost unopposed, but their commander digs in, and the Germans seal the beachhead.

headline: Roosevelt creates the War Refugee Board
detail: Prodded by Treasury officials who accuse the State Department of obstructing rescue, Roosevelt sets up a body to save Jews and other victims of the Nazis.

headline: Siege of Leningrad lifted after 872 days
detail: The city celebrates with a 324-gun salute over the Neva. Perhaps a million civilians have died, most of hunger and cold.

headline: Two German corps trapped in the Korsun pocket
detail: Soviet pincers close around German troops on the Dnieper. Thousands will die in a desperate breakout through the snow in February.

headline: Americans land in the Marshall Islands
detail: Landings at Majuro and Kwajalein atolls begin the drive through the central Pacific. Lessons from Tarawa keep losses lower.

headline: Japanese offensive in Arakan meets the "Admin Box"
detail: Surrounded Indian and British troops, supplied by air, refuse to retreat. The Japanese attack collapses for lack of food and ammunition.

headline: Colossus breaks its first German message
detail: At Bletchley Park the first Colossus, an electronic machine with some 1,600 valves, begins attacking German teleprinter ciphers.

headline: Bombers destroy the abbey of Monte Cassino
detail: Over 200 Allied bombers reduce the 6th-century Benedictine monastery to rubble. German paratroopers then occupy the ruins.

headline: US carrier raid wrecks the Japanese base at Truk
detail: Operation Hailstone sinks dozens of ships and destroys hundreds of aircraft at Japan's main fleet anchorage in the central Pacific.

headline: RAF Mosquitos breach the walls of Amiens prison
detail: Operation Jericho frees about 255 prisoners, many of them résistants, but some 102 prisoners die in the bombing.

headline: Ferry carrying heavy water sunk in Lake Tinn
detail: Norwegian saboteurs sink the Hydro with its cargo bound for Germany. Fourteen Norwegian crew and passengers and four German soldiers die.

headline: "Big Week" air offensive against German aircraft factories
detail: American and British bombers begin six days of attacks on the Luftwaffe's factories, while escort fighters wear down its pilots.

headline: Stalin deports the Chechen and Ingush peoples
detail: In a single operation the NKVD loads close to half a million people onto trains bound for Central Asia. Many thousands die on the way and after.

headline: US troops land in the Admiralty Islands
detail: A reconnaissance in force on Los Negros turns into a full invasion, completing the isolation of Rabaul.

headline: Chindits fly into Burma by glider
detail: Operation Thursday lands Wingate's second expedition deep behind Japanese lines at jungle clearings called Broadway and Chowringhee.

headline: First major American daylight raid on Berlin
detail: Some 660 heavy bombers attack the German capital with fighter escort. Sixty-nine bombers are lost, but the Luftwaffe loses more pilots than it can replace.

headline: Japan launches its march on India
detail: Operation U-Go: the Fifteenth Army crosses towards Imphal and Kohima, counting on captured British supplies to feed its men.

headline: Cassino town flattened by bombers and guns
detail: Hundreds of aircraft and artillery pieces pulverise the town before New Zealand and Indian troops attack. German paratroopers hold out in the rubble.

headline: Vesuvius erupts behind the Allied lines
detail: The volcano's last eruption to date buries villages under ash and destroys some 80 American bombers on an airfield near Pompeii.

headline: Germany occupies Hungary
detail: Hitler sends troops into his wavering ally. Adolf Eichmann arrives with an SS team to organise the deportation of Hungary's Jews.

headline: SS massacre 335 men in Rome's Ardeatine Caves
detail: In reprisal for a partisan bombing in the Via Rasella, Italian men and boys, many of them Jews and political prisoners, are shot.

headline: Orde Wingate killed in an air crash
detail: The Chindit commander dies when his B-25 crashes in the hills of north-east India, weeks into his second expedition.

headline: Seventy-six airmen tunnel out of Stalag Luft III
detail: In the 'Great Escape', 73 are recaptured. On Hitler's order, fifty of them are murdered by the Gestapo. Only three reach freedom.

headline: Battle of Kohima begins
detail: The Japanese 31st Division reaches the hill station. About 2,500 defenders, many of them non-combatants, are soon surrounded.

headline: Two prisoners escape Auschwitz to warn the world
detail: Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler hide in a woodpile for three days, then flee to Slovakia. Their report describes the gas chambers in detail.

headline: Odessa liberated
detail: The Red Army retakes the Black Sea port after two and a half years of Romanian and German occupation.

headline: Ship explosion devastates Bombay docks
detail: The freighter Fort Stikine, carrying explosives and cotton, blows up in Victoria Dock, killing some 800 people and wrecking the port.

headline: Japan opens Operation Ichi-Go in China
detail: Japanese troops cross the Yellow River in Henan in the largest offensive in the Japanese army's history, aimed at China's railways and airfields.

headline: Kohima garrison relieved
detail: Tanks and Indian infantry break through to Garrison Hill. The battle for the ridges goes on for two more months.

headline: MacArthur leaps to Hollandia
detail: American troops land at Hollandia and Aitape on New Guinea's north coast, bypassing and stranding tens of thousands of Japanese soldiers.

headline: German general kidnapped on Crete
detail: British SOE officers and Cretan partisans seize General Heinrich Kreipe near Knossos and smuggle him over the mountains to Egypt.

headline: E-boats strike a D-Day rehearsal in Lyme Bay
detail: German torpedo boats attack landing ships during Exercise Tiger. At least 749 American servicemen die. The disaster is kept secret.

headline: Sevastopol liberated
detail: The Red Army retakes the Crimean fortress city in a few days. The Germans had needed eight months to capture it.

headline: Allies launch the final assault on the Gustav Line
detail: Operation Diadem opens with a barrage from some 1,600 guns along the front from Cassino to the sea.

headline: Chinese troops cross the Salween into Burma
detail: The American-trained Chinese Y Force attacks westward to reopen the land route to China.

headline: Deportation of Hungary's Jews begins
detail: Trains start for Auschwitz-Birkenau. By 9 July more than 434,000 people are deported; most are murdered on arrival.

headline: Allied force seizes Myitkyina airfield
detail: Merrill's Marauders and Chinese troops take the airfield in northern Burma after a march across the Kumon mountains.

headline: Poles raise their flag over Monte Cassino
detail: Polish II Corps takes the abbey ruins at the cost of nearly a thousand dead. The Gustav Line is broken.

headline: Stalin deports the Crimean Tatars
detail: In under three days the NKVD sends almost the entire Crimean Tatar nation by train to Central Asia. Many thousands die within a year.

headline: Allies break out of the Anzio beachhead
detail: After four months penned in, the troops at Anzio attack as the Gustav Line crumbles. The road to Rome opens.

headline: Japanese troops capture Luoyang
detail: The ancient city in Henan falls after a two-week siege, as Operation Ichi-Go sweeps through central China.

headline: Americans land on Biak
detail: US troops land on the island off New Guinea to seize its airfields, and meet fierce resistance from caves and ridges.

headline: Rome liberated
detail: American troops enter the Eternal City, the first Axis capital to fall. Retreating German forces leave it undamaged.

headline: US Navy captures U-505 at sea
detail: A hunter-killer group off West Africa forces the U-boat to the surface and boards her, seizing codebooks and an Enigma machine.

headline: Eisenhower gives the order: the invasion goes ahead
detail: After a one-day delay for storms, Eisenhower decides to sail. That evening he visits paratroopers of the 101st Airborne at Greenham Common.

headline: D-Day: Allied forces land in Normandy
detail: Gliders seize the Orne bridges after midnight. By nightfall some 156,000 Allied troops are ashore on five beaches.
